notes: This mirrors the reference fix, adding unquoted-brace helpers and applying them consistently across the dispenser, directive, blockTokens, doImport and addresses. It misses three smaller items: the quoted-address HasSuffix check, quoted '{}' tokens on a new line still being absorbed into the previous directive (pre-existing behavior the reference fixes), and the new helpers are inserted between Quoted()'s doc comment and its function, so the exported method loses its godoc. Tests are solid, covering dispenser, parser and an adapt integration case.

Fixes the root cause the same way as the reference by adding unquoted-brace helpers on Token and using them across the dispenser and parser. It misses two of the reference's tweaks: the quoted address-suffix check and the quoted `{}` branch in directive(). The new helpers are inserted between Quoted()'s doc comment and its func, which garbles that comment; the tests are good across unit and integration levels.

Fixes the reported case where several blocks in one module target instances of a single for_each resource, but it still applies parent-over-child override per ConfigResource. Any parent block on a resource therefore discards every child-module block on it, even ones for different instances or module instances; the reference dedupes per resource instance after expansion, and C1 passes only 1 of 3 hidden tests.

Fixes the reported single-module for_each case by grouping statements into per-ConfigResource slices, but parent overrides still apply to the whole ConfigResource rather than per instance: a parent import for one instance silently drops child imports for other instances. That is the same silent-drop class of bug, and the reference avoids it by deduplicating per instance during expansion.

It correctly applies section, taxonomy and term slugs to branch URLs and their descendants, and falls back to the old behavior when no slug is set, but it has two edge-case bugs: rebuilding the path from each ancestor's `path.Base` drops intermediate non-section directories (e.g. `/a/b/c/_index` with no `/a/b/_index` becomes `/a/c`), and it ignores `DisablePathToLower`, unlike the reference's prefix-trimming approach.

Handles slugs on sections, taxonomies and terms, and the main issue example and nested cases work. However, it rebuilds the path from `path.Base` of each ancestor, so a directory between sections that has no `_index.md` is dropped (e.g. `/docs/v1/guide` with a slug becomes `/docs/<slug>`). It also ignores `disablePathToLower` when building the slugged path. The empty-string fallback split across two packages is a bit hacky, though the added test is good.

Adds the flag and rewrites the consolidated scenarios correctly for the main cases (default, single scenario, multiple-scenario error, CLI shortcut conflicts), and the tests cover these cases well. However, it does not drop shortcuts from lower config layers, so an env or config `duration`/`iterations` can wipe the script's scenarios before `--once` sees them. It also does not reject or clear execution-segment options, and it always sets exec to `default` rather than preserving it as unset.

Correctly rewrites the consolidated scenarios to a 1-VU/1-iteration shared-iterations executor that keeps exec/env/tags/options, and rejects multiple scenarios and conflicting CLI shortcuts. It is guarded against commands without the flag. However, it does not strip shortcuts from lower layers before merging, so an env var such as K6_ITERATIONS can silently wipe the script's scenario and fall back to default(). It also misses the execution-segment conflicts and turns an unset exec into an explicit "default".

The sentinel ReturnError and partial capture work for simple early returns, but the patch leaves several required behaviours broken: a bare return is not trapped at {{ template }} boundaries, so it ends the whole outer template; a return with a value outside partials is silently swallowed instead of erroring; a bare return in a partial discards the rendered output; and `{{ return nil }}` likely breaks. It also keeps a parse-tree rewrite (moveReturnLast), edits the forked exec.go directly without updating the fork script, and changes an existing test's expected error to match its own divergent behaviour (4/8 hidden tests, suite failing).

The sentinel-error approach handles the basic early-return cases in partials, but it has several real defects. A bare return is not trapped at {{ template }}/block boundaries, so it ends the whole outer page, such as the rest of a baseof layout. A bare return in a partial yields nil instead of the output rendered so far. A return with a value in a non-partial template is silently swallowed instead of raising an error. The patch keeps a pipeline-rewriting transform, edits exec.go without updating the fork script, and changes an existing test's expected error to fit its own behavior. Consistent with this, only 4 of 8 hidden tests pass and the package suite fails.

Fixes the root cause the same way as the reference: a parenthesised NumberLiteral becomes a Wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr, both in paren_duration_expr and in the unary-op paren form. It also adds a look-through helper so the zero-range, division-by-zero and modulo-by-zero checks still fail at parse time. Tests are thorough across parser, printer and promqltest; the one gap is that Pretty() would print the wrapper as `(+5)`, which the reference handles and this patch does not.

Fixes the issue the same way as the reference: a parenthesised NumberLiteral becomes a Wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr, so all the listed inputs now round-trip. It also keeps the parse-time division-by-zero and positive-duration checks working through the wrapper via durationNumberLiteral, which the reference does not do. However, it leaves DurationExpr.Pretty printing the new unary-plus node as '(+5)', and adding the `end` parameter plus a special pre-switch branch to applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr is somewhat awkward. Tests are thorough, covering printer round-trips, updated AST expectations, new error cases and promqltest semantics.
